description: cd2es provides a Python and Snakemake workflow for converting climate projections into energy-system model inputs. Ruhr University Bochum publishes the software to assess how changing climate conditions alter renewable generation and other energy-system time series. The documented workflow uses CORDEX model outputs and can optionally adjust their bias against ERA5 reanalysis. It produces renewable capacity factors, demand series and thermal-power-plant availability at hourly resolution, aggregated to geometries chosen by the user. Geographic coverage and future periods depend on the selected climate projection and input area. Zenodo provides the public v1.2 code archive and metadata under GPL-3.0-or-later, allowing free software reuse. The linked university GitLab API returned a server error during this review, so verification rests on the archived software record. Climate-model assumptions and upstream data access remain application-specific limitations. The outputs can support capacity planning and climate-sensitivity scenarios. Related record model-pypsa is an energy-system modeller that could use suitable time-series inputs; a direct interface was not verified. Neither source climate data nor the code archive was downloaded.
